why: `nros::Seq<T, N>` -- a fixed-capacity inline sequence, the `no_std` stand-in for `std::vector<T>` at the parameter surface, so a ported rclcpp node that declares a `std::vector<double>` weight matrix (RFC-0044 Q3, phase 242.3) compiles with no heap. Constraint: no allocator. Over-capacity is rejected or flagged (`overflowed()`), never UB. Under `NROS_CPP_STD` it converts to and from `std::vector<T>` so hosted source is unchanged. rclcpp needs no counterpart because `std::vector` is always available to it. Element types are `double`/`int64_t`/`bool` only -- there is no `Seq` path for the `byte_array` or `string_array` parameter types the C layer underneath does support (`rclc_parameter_declare_byte_array`, `rclc_parameter_declare_string_array`), so C++ reaches 8 of the 10 `rcl_interfaces` types. PHASE-426 W4 (2026-09-11) -- WHAT IT IS A VALUE FOR CHANGED, and this is the reason the type outlived the class it shipped with. `nros::ParameterServer<Cap>` is deleted (see that row); `Seq` was its element-carrying value and is now the node API's: `node.declare_parameter(name, Seq<double, 8>{...})` / `get_parameter(name, seq)` / `set_parameter(name, seq)` route through `nros_cpp_node_{declare,get,set}_param_{double,integer,bool}_array` onto the executor's store, so a sequence parameter is visible to `ros2 param get` like every scalar. Three things follow. The ELEMENTS are owned by the store (a `heapless::Vec` in its slot), not by an inline bump pool in the header, so there is no borrow for the caller to outlive -- `ParameterServer`'s `seq_pool_` left with the class. The overloads sit OUTSIDE `NROS_CPP_STD`, deliberately: `Seq` is the array form a `-nostdinc++` node has, because `std::vector<T>` reaches the same FFI only under that macro. And a read into a too-small `Seq` is refused (`ErrorCode::Full`) rather than truncated, matching the `std::vector` read's two-call length probe -- a short weight matrix is a plausible wrong answer, which is worse than an error. `Seq<bool, N>` exists where `std::vector<bool>` cannot: its storage is a plain `bool[N]`, so it has a `data()`. Phase 379 W3.
